title: Duration and the PRC matrix
objectives: Use modified duration to estimate a price move for a 1% rate change.
Read a debt scheme's PRC cell, and say how it differs from the riskometer.
body_md:
Duration in one line: a fund's modified duration tells you roughly how much its price moves for a 1% change in rates. Duration 4 → rates up 1% means price down about 4%; rates down 1% means price up about 4%. Every debt scheme also discloses the maximum interest-rate and credit risk it is allowed to take, as a cell in SEBI's 3×3 Potential Risk Class (PRC) matrix: interest-rate Classes I (Macaulay duration up to 1 year), II (up to 3 years), III (any duration) against credit Classes A (relatively low), B (moderate), C (relatively high). A-I is the most conservative cell; C-III the most aggressive. The PRC shows the scheme's limit; the riskometer shows its current portfolio. Check both.

| Interest-rate risk ↓ / Credit risk → | Class A: relatively low | Class B: moderate | Class C: relatively high |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Class I (Macaulay duration up to 1 year) | A-I | B-I | C-I |
| Class II (up to 3 years) | A-II | B-II | C-II |
| Class III (any duration) | A-III | B-III | C-III |

> **Investor takeaway:** Duration should match the goal date; credit quality should match how essential the money is.
example: Duration 6, rates fall 1%: price rises about 6%. A scheme in cell C-III may take relatively high credit risk at any duration.
say: PRC is the limit; the riskometer is the portfolio today. Check both.
A-I is the most conservative PRC cell.
never: A-III is more conservative than A-I.

check.q: A fund with modified duration 6 will, if rates fall 1%, roughly:
check.why: Rise 6%. Price moves opposite to rates by about the duration.

check.q: The most conservative cell in the PRC matrix is:
check.why: A-I. Low credit risk, duration up to 1 year.

check.q: The PRC matrix shows a debt scheme's:
check.why: Maximum interest-rate and credit risk. The riskometer shows today's portfolio risk.
